description: Rebuild all 99 candidate polygons from B16+B34+B35+B36+B37+B38+B42. Confirm B45 T/O steepest-descent exits against periodically wrapped full-world landmask at 6- and 3-unit planar raster resolution. No new coastline changes.
applied_layers: B45 replay synthetic T/O drainage directly from saved formula (no terrain edits)

sampling.water_connectivity: 4-neighbor flood-fill from upper and lower outer frame water cells; x wraps by 2400 drawing units. This is projected raster connectivity, not measured ocean depth, global geophysical proof or navigability.
sampling.B45_D8: Recomputed full B45 T/O float synthetic heights and 8-direction steepest descent; first grid cell outside polygon #0 classified through entire reconstructed global land mask.

limits: Raster land mask tests water connectivity on a finite working map, not actual terrestrial shoreline, depth or current regime.
4-connectivity and the 3/6 illustration-unit spacing could miss sub-grid barriers, underwater obstacles and narrow channels.
B45 elevation/flow algorithm is synthetic; confirming that its first water pixels connect to edge water does not validate the river courses.
Global frame top/bottom are used as water-component seeds purely for cartographic topology; real polar bathymetry not represented.
All 25 accepted ocean/sea names, country positions and North Crown physical constraints remain unchanged.
No Zangshuoyuan sea or anomalous-water network is assigned to current coordinates in B46; separate future study.
next: B47: inspect specific coast-exit concentration points and overly large synthetic drainage funnels; no river-channel claims until relief hypotheses are constrained.
Investigate model assumptions for highlands, resistance arc, erosion and sediment without treating arbitrary relief peaks as real mountains.
Maintain B42 coastline and preserve 99 land shapes while studying catchment route sensitivity.
